claims: tier2's reordering doesn't reach what gets stored (`tier2-light-forensic.mjs:672-682`, caused by the change at `:394-395`): the write step builds `new Set([...existingEntry.tags, ...derived.tags]).slice(0, 20)`, so stored tier1 tags come first; for the 81 addresses with >15 tags at most two `ctp:` tags survive and `type:contract` is lost every time

`--limit` / `--quota-floor` with a missing value is silently ignored (`tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:112-126`): `flagValue` returns `undefined` both when the flag is absent and when its value is missing, so `--limit --no-refresh` runs with no limit and can sweep the whole ~68k queue

A source that hits the page cap still counts as complete (`tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:284-287`): on `capped: true` the script only prints a warning and never adds the source to `failedSources`, so the abort-on-incomplete-discovery check doesn't apply and quota is spent on a truncated set

The quota floor is only checked every 500 addresses when Remaining comes from the API body (`tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:1000`, `:1058`): without the `X-Intel-Datapoints-Remaining` header, remaining can go from ~500 to 0 between polls and the run ends on a 402/403 halt instead of stopping cleanly above the floor
A leftover comment contradicts the corrected header (`run.sh:44`): the inline comment still says "A dry run touches neither Arkham nor Upstash", which lines 15-19 now contradict
File-size budget: tier1 grows from 474 to 1,088 raw lines, and the checklist (`recurring-review-patterns.md:204-206`) says a file pushed past 600 lines should be split in the same PR
Progress written before the batched write is flushed: a crash can lose up to 99 results that resume will then skip (pre-existing at base)

judge_reasoning.3845594538: No match. The review's only related note is that progress is written before the flush, so a crash can lose results. It dismisses that as pre-existing and never identifies splice-before-network dropping batches on a transient pipeline failure.
judge_reasoning.3845596185: Match. Review finding 3 says a source returning capped: true is only warned about and never added to failedSources, so the incomplete-discovery abort doesn't fire.

1.why: tier2-light-forensic.mjs:672-682 puts the stored tags ahead of derived.tags before .slice(0,20). This is the same issue as the known 'Preserve Tier 2 tags when merging capped labels' (tier2:395).

2.why: At tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:113-117, flagValue returns undefined when the next arg starts with '--'. numericFlag then uses the fallback (Infinity for --limit), so `--limit --no-refresh` quietly runs with no limit, even though numericFlag is documented as failing hard on bad input.

3.why: At :284-287, capped only adds a warning to the log line and is never pushed to failedSources. This matches the known HARD_PAGE_CAP truncation defects (:311/:328).

4.why: quota.remaining is only updated from the body when there's no Remaining header, and logIntelUsage runs only every INTEL_USAGE_EVERY=500 addresses (:1058). The floor check at :1000 can therefore use a stale value and miss the default floor of 50, so the run ends on the 402/403 halt instead of stopping cleanly.

5.why: The diff adds the run.sh:44 comment 'A dry run touches neither Arkham nor Upstash', but the new header at lines 15-19 says the dry run DOES use Upstash and still mints a REST token.

6.why: The file did grow from 474 to 1088 lines, but recurring-review-patterns.md:204 calls the 600-line limit a 'soft cap, advisory'. That makes this a style/process note, not a functional defect.

7.why: Progress is appended at :1010 before the batched flush, and base does the same (base lines 382/392). The claim itself says this predates the change, so it isn't a defect this change introduced.
